purpose: Record a source-named Quezon river lead and a bounded fish occurrence text search without inferring fish absence, river geometry, or equivalence with Hinabaan River.

sourceReviews.title: CALABARZON Monitor, April-June 2005
sourceReviews.finding: Indexed text from the official DENR-EMB CALABARZON bulletin names Viñas River with the parenthetical locality Guinayangan-Tagkawayan, Quezon, and contains the statement that fishing is noted as its most beneficial use. Direct PDF access returned HTTP 403, so only this indexed excerpt was reviewed.
sourceReviews.decision: Add a source-named river research lead only. Do not interpret the beneficial-use statement as a current legal classification, public access right, fish record, or geometry.

sourceReviews.title: NGA Pub. 162, Sailing Directions (Enroute) Philippine Islands, 14th edition, 2025
sourceReviews.finding: Official indexed text describes Vinas River at an approximate mouth position and says it extends about four miles northwest from the outer bar. The official 2025 edition and corrected-to date were confirmed in NGA publication search results. The direct PDF reader refused the 11 MB document as too large.
sourceReviews.decision: Independent nautical name/route context only. Do not treat the rounded position as a surveyed point or the route text as a river centerline, legal line, current survey, or proof that Vinas and Hinabaan are the same feature.

sourceReviews.title: GBIF occurrence API selected CoL XR Actinopterygii search
sourceReviews.finding: Four requests searched the exact accented and unaccented names in waterBody and locality for country PH with the selected CoL XR Actinopterygii filters. All returned HTTP 200 and zero indexed matches.
sourceReviews.decision: Bounded indexed-text search only. Zero results do not establish fish absence and do not replace locality variants, all-taxon discovery, or a station-resolved survey.

taxonomy.label: Catalogue of Life Extended Release Actinopterygii

identityCrosswalk.status: unresolved; not merged; no alias assigned
identityCrosswalk.reason: The official bulletin names Viñas River with Guinayangan-Tagkawayan context, while the existing Hinabaan lead is separately source-named at Balinarin/Hinabaan. NGA provides approximate nautical route context for Vinas River but not a relationship to Hinabaan; no authoritative crosswalk reconciles the feature names or reaches.

limitations: The official EMB bulletin PDF could not be opened directly; the name and short beneficial-use context are from indexed text only. The 2025 NGA PDF was too large for the web reader, so its name/route context is from official indexed text.
The bulletin excerpt is not a species survey and contains no station-resolved fish record, current condition, coordinates, or channel route.
The four GBIF zero results are bounded indexed-field searches and do not establish fish absence.
Possible overlap with Hinabaan River remains unresolved; no alias or geometry is inferred. The rounded nautical position and route description are not digitized.
No current salinity, fishing access, legal classification, safety, or reuse permission is established.
nextAction: Seek a retrievable DENR-EMB waterbody classification record or an authoritative LGU/NAMRIA feature-name and route source that can resolve Viñas River identity and possible overlap with Hinabaan; find a station-resolved fish survey with reviewable reuse terms before adding fish evidence.
